title: PoeLLM malware exploits Python Poetry in 3,000+ server compromise
summary: PoeLLM malware has compromised over 3,000 servers since April 2026 by exploiting Python Poetry and using "adversarial poetry"—AI jailbreak techniques embedding harmful prompts in poems to evade detection. The malware primarily targets open-source AI systems like LiteLLM and Ollama, aiming for crypto
takeaways: 3,000+ servers compromised since April 2026
Peak activity: 800+ active servers infected daily
Primary targets: LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg, Gitea, Ivanti Sentry
First real-world use of adversarial poetry as attack method
Suspected Italian attacker; malware hides C2 info in GitHub poems
3,400+ servers infected; peak mid-June: 2,200 servers, 800 daily active

title: Multimodal AI Startup Jev Reaches $7.5B Valuation Weeks After Launch
summary: TypeSafe AI's Jev, a non-text AI model based on transformer architecture, reached a $7.5 billion valuation weeks after its September 15, 2026 launch, raising $870 million led by Andreessen Horowitz. The model produces calibrated probabilities rather than text, operates significantly faster than LLMs
takeaways: Jev launched September 15, 2026; raised $870 million at $7.5 billion valuation weeks later
Series led by Andreessen Horowitz with Sequoia and DCVC participation
Non-text transformer model producing calibrated probabilities rather than text output
Works significantly faster and uses far fewer tokens than LLMs; positioned for automation tasks
One-third of Fortune 500 already using Jev; founded 2024 by former OpenAI and Meta researchers

title: LLM-jacking emerges as major AI cybercrime with doubled underground prices
summary: LLM-jacking, a cybercrime involving theft of cloud credentials to illegally access and monetize paid language models, has emerged as a distinct threat targeting Amazon Bedrock and Google Vertex AI. Underground prices for hijacked AI infrastructure have doubled through 2026.
takeaways: LLM-jacking involves stealing IAM access keys to run paid models at victim's expense
Recent documented cases: Amazon Bedrock and Google Vertex AI compromises
Underground prices for hijacked AI infrastructure doubled through 2026
CERT-EU's September 2026 report flagged surge in LLM-jacking incidents across Europe
AI infrastructure now both a tool for and target of cybercriminals

title: Chutes and Harvard Release 6.12 Billion LLM Request Dataset
summary: Chutes AI and Harvard researchers published a year-long production trace of 6.12 billion LLM inference requests from April 2025 to April 2026, covering 9,174 models served to 314,970 users. The 91 GB dataset excludes prompts and outputs for privacy, offering the AI infrastructure research community
takeaways: Dataset contains 6.12 billion LLM inference requests from April 11, 2025 through April 12, 2026
Covers 9,174 distinct models served across 314,970 users with 35.8 trillion input tokens processed
Stripped of prompts, responses, and tool calls; retains infrastructure metadata (timestamps, token counts, cache hits, latency)
91 GB Parquet file hosted on Harvard servers with companion arXiv paper
Three orders of magnitude larger than typical public LLM datasets, which usually number in the millions of interactions
